σάνδυξ , υκος, ἡ,
A.a bright red colour, also called ἀρμένιον, Str. 11.14.9 (prob. cj.); obtained by heating ψιμύθιον ( = cerussa), Dsc. 5.88 , cf. Plin. HN 35.40 ; though a like colour was made from a plant of the same name, red sandalwood, Pterocarpus santalinus,
Sosib. 21 , Verg. Ecl. 4.45 , Plin. l.c., Lyd. Mag. 3.64 .
2. pl., flesh-coloured women's garments dyed with this colour, in Lydia, ibid.
3. a kind of salve, prob. a pink mixture of zinc oxide and carbonate, Dsc. l.c., Gal. 12.244 , Hsch.
II. casket, Id. [ū in genit., Pro p.2.19.81 ; but [ucaron] in Grattius Cyn. 86 .] (Assyr. sâmtu, sându 'red stone', prob. cinnabar.)
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
